newsitem.title: USA: Stocks fall on profit-taking, bonds unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Stocks fall on profit-taking, bonds unchanged.

text.p: Blue-chip stocks fell Wednesday as investors took profits after the previous day's rally, while bonds ended barely changed.
The dollar fell as mounting uncertainty ahead of runoff elections in France strengthened the German mark and the outlook for higher Japanese interest rates boosted the yen.
The Dow Jones industrial average lost 26.18 points to close at 7,357.23, a day after jumping 38 points to a record 7,383.41, its sixth milestone this month and the 21st of the year.
But the Nasdaq composite index eked out a gain of 0.97 of a point to 1,410.18, topping Tuesday's record as investors were again drawn to high-technology and some smaller stocks.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,310 to 1,150 on active volume of 487 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said investors who have been buying blue-chips turned cautious as interest rates kept rising in the bond market.

"For the last few days, people thought short-term rates were not going to rise, but they edged up. That can hurt equities performance," said Michael Metz, chief investment officer at Oppenheimer & Co.
"A lot of portfolio managers are peeling back their blue chip holdings a little, because they have run very far, very fast," said Metz.
The yield on the benchmark 30-year Treasury stayed above 7 percent, a level that tends to draw funds away from stocks.

Investors were also trying to make sense of the latest economic data. The government said orders for costly manufactured goods rose in April after falling in March but lower order backlogs pointed to slower growth ahead.
The Commerce Department said durable goods orders rose 1.4 percent, the third increase in the past four months, following a revised 2.2 percent drop in March.
In late New York trading, the dollar fetched 1.6956 marks, down from 1.7055 marks late Tuesday. The dollar fell to 115.85 Japanese yen from 116.67 yen.
At the Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange in New York, coffee for July delivery closed 21.25 cents a pound higher at 295.55 cents, just below a 20-year high of 297.00 cents reached earlier in the day.

At the New York Mercantile Exchange, palladium prices soared to a 17-year high as the market's nerve finally snapped on news of a strike in South Africa amid tight physical supplies. Palladium for June delivery settled $28.15 higher at $202.65 an ounce, just off the day's high of $204.00.
NYMEX platinum for July delivery settled $13.50 firmer at $410.50 an ounce, after ranging from $396.50 to $411.00.
Crude oil futures at the NYMEX ended little changed after a slow session following Tuesday's steep losses.

Crude oil for July delivery closed unchanged at $20.79 a barrel, with June unleaded gasoline ending 0.42 cent a gallon higher at 65.80 cents and June heating oil ending up 0.12 cent a gallon at 55.39 cents.

Overseas, London's FTSE 100 index slipped 4.1 points to close at 4,677.5. In Tokyo, the 225-share Nikkei average surged 461.45 points, or 2.32 percent, to finish at 20,351.34, just below the day's high of 20,351.64.
